title: What’s the point of MIT? OpenAI’s math proofs have thrown students and researchers into chaos.
key_facts: OpenAI announced on 8 Sep 2026 that its AI agents solved one of the Millennium Prize Problems (Navier-Stokes), each worth $1 million.
Last week OpenAI published proofs for nearly 400 more previously unsolved problems; the Globe says significance and accuracy will take time to sort out.
MIT maths department held a gathering of 100+ students, professors and postdocs to discuss AI.
Survey of the department (45 of 120 responded): three in four feared harder tenure-track job prospects; 71% were looking to pivot.
MIT's August report found AI agents could complete any written undergraduate assignment.
Professor Pavel Etingof expects the role of mathematicians to shift toward interpreting and communicating AI-made proofs.
quote_evidence: It will take some time to sort out the significance, and accuracy, of these proofs.
Three out of four respondents said they feared AI will make it harder to get a tenure-track job.
The majority of participants (71 percent) were now looking to pivot, responding that their chances of continuing into “academic math” had decreased.
why_it_matters_hint: AI results in pure maths are hitting early-career researchers’ hopes.
event_date: 8 Sep 2026 (OpenAI announcement); campus reaction reported 15 Oct 2026
notes: The Globe says the gathering took place two days after 8 Sep but also says proofs came "last week"; the sequence of dates in the article is unclear.
